title: The feature describes the vendor choice as distance and capacity while the two rules it names allocate on the scorecard predicted price and not by distance
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E4-023, its Story paragraph and Acceptance criteria AC1, AC2 and AC3); Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (A2.14.1 business objective, A2.14.2 functional overview, A2.14.3.1 rule table); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (rows R-DIS-30 and R-DIS-31); Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 (feature row FEAT-AST-14)
section: APP s2 Business rationale; s4 Flow steps 6 and 9; s5 X8; s7 note on AC1 and AC2; s8 BR7; s9 State transitions; s13 Configuration; CON s2, s7 AC5 and s12.5
description: Two bases for one selection are stated in the same sources. The legacy story says the Workbench picks one of the four vendors by distance and capacity as the current rule does, the FSD A2.14.1 and A2.14.2 repeat that wording as the business objective and the functional overview, and FEAT-AST-14 of the feature extract carries the same sentence. AC2, AC3, the FSD rule table and the Business Rules and Routing Logic give the two rules the step evaluates a different basis: R-DIS-30 allocates the asset to the vendor with the highest predicted price on the scorecard, not by distance, when asset_type = vehicle, and R-DIS-31 re-allocates to the next vendor on the scorecard when vendor_capacity = N or panel_status = suspended. The distance is not a field of any rule row and no source states which basis applies when the asset is not a vehicle.
evidence: Legacy AC1 Then line: picks one of the four vendors by distance and capacity, as the current rule does. Legacy AC2 Then line: allocate the asset to the vendor with the highest predicted price on the scorecard, not by distance. Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DIS-30 condition asset_type = vehicle and action Allocate the asset to the vendor with the highest predicted price on the scorecard, not by distance; R-DIS-31 action Re-allocate to the next vendor on the scorecard. FSD S5 A2.14.2 functional overview: Picks one of the four vendors by distance and capacity, as the current rule does. Neither the FSD rule table nor the rule workbook gives a rule row for an asset that is not a vehicle.
owner_role: S5 rwb-asset service owner with the rule owner of the DISPOSAL route set in P7
proposed: Keep both statements, let the rule row decide the basis, and carry the distance and the capacity as rule inputs read with their version; the non-vehicle basis stays unstated and is raised as a gap until a rule row names it.

title: The trigger of the step, the vendor-panel facts and the partner activity have no published operation, no event and no row in the plan dependency lists
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E4-023, its Story paragraph, Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC4, Endpoints and Permission checks); Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (A2.14.2 steps, integration points Partner portal, A2.14.3.3 roles, A2.14.4.4 no background event); Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (T5.1, T5.2, T5.3, appendix T-A.1); _work/msr/context/S5.md (ownership rows of S5: two tables, six REST operations, one event, one job, one workflow; connection matrix row S5 Asset); _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json (both slices of RWB-E4-023: H, C, I and X lists)
section: APP s1 Story; s2 Business rationale; s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow steps 2, 4 and 9; s5 X4 and X6; s10 Authority; s11 Data; s12.2; s12.4; s12.5; s12.8; s13 Solution plan; s19 Out of scope; CON s3, s7 AC3 and AC4, s11 Data, s12.2, s12.4, s12.5, s12.8, s13, s19
description: The step has no single stated trigger and no stated source for the panel it allocates from. The legacy AC1 says When its trigger arrives and AC2 and AC3 say When vendor required and When vendor unavailable, the FSD A2.14.2 names the trigger as a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer and A2.14.4.4 declares no background event, and TSD S5 T5.3 gives the module one published event and no consumed one. The facts the two rules test are spread over three owners: asset_type and the scorecard predicted price are the ACE facts of v_ace_npa_asset and v_ace_score, vendor_capacity and panel_status are partner facts, and the four-vendor list is the parameter and reference-data row of FEAT-PRM-03 that the legacy story names as its dependency. The connection matrix gives S5 to S9 a Temporal call and to P7 a Temporal call, with no REST row, and the architecture notes say route services reach shared capabilities through Temporal and never REST, so a REST read of the panel would contradict the matrix. No source publishes the operation of the partner instruction or panel read, no source gives the panel field names, and the plan carries no C row and no X row for either slice.
evidence: Context pack ownership rows of S5: tables asset_sale and listing, six REST operations, events EV-22, jobs JOB-19, workflows AssetDisposalWorkflow. Connection matrix row S5 Asset marks P7 T, S4 E, P8 T E, S9 T E and no R anywhere. TSD S5 T5.3 lists AssetTakenOn published and no consumed event; T-A.1 lists five endpoints, none of them a vendor or allocation operation. Legacy metadata Depends on FEAT-PRM-03; FSD A2.14.3.3 gives the primary role as None; runs unattended. Plan slices RWB-S5-E4023-APP and RWB-S5-E4023-CON carry C, I and X as empty lists.
owner_role: S5 rwb-asset service owner with the owners of S9 rwb-partner, P1 rwb-source-data and P3 rwb-case
proposed: Read the two triggers as signals of the DISPOSAL machine forwarded by the parent CaseWorkflow, read the panel on the rwb-partner activity of queue rwb-partner, read the asset and score facts on the rwb-source-data data product, treat all of them as class C dependencies the plan does not carry, and register a C row for the key at the next plan revision.

title: The allocation has no column, no list value and no owned row, and the two tables of the service carry no vendor, distance or allocation state
source: _work/msr/context/S5.md (ownership rows of S5: tables asset_sale and listing); Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (T3.1 listing and asset_sale field definitions, T3.2 LOV-SALE-CHANNEL and LOV-HOLDING, T3.3 relationships); Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (A2.14.2 step 3 writes the decision log entry); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E4-023, Data table and Screen and states table)
section: APP s2 Business rationale; s8 BR1 and BR5; s9 State transitions; s11 Data; s12.7; s13 Database and migrations; s19; CON s11 Data, s12.7, s13
description: The outcome of R-DIS-30 and R-DIS-31 is a vendor and a basis, and the data model of the target does not hold either. The ownership rows of S5 give the service two tables, asset_sale and listing; listing carries sale_channel, start_price, floor_price, round_no, listed_at and status, and asset_sale carries the sale, its prices, its taxes and its gain or loss. LOV-SALE-CHANNEL is DUTCH_AUCTION, BROKER, DIRECT, LED_AUCTION and RAMC, with no vendor value, and LOV-HOLDING is HELD, LISTED, UNDER_OFFER, SOLD, TRANSFERRED and RENTED, with no allocated state. The legacy Data table names no table of the service at all and sends the result to decision_log_entry, and the legacy story's own step 3 records the result and writes the decision log entry. The vendor reference, the distance and the allocation state therefore have no home in rwb_asset, and a new column or a new list value would be a data-model change no source authorises.
evidence: TSD S5 T3.1 gives listing the eight fields DF-SAL-001 to DF-SAL-008 and asset_sale the eleven fields DF-SAL-009 to DF-SAL-019, with no vendor, distance, score or allocation field in either. TSD S5 T3.2 LOV-SALE-CHANNEL has five values and LOV-HOLDING six, none of them a vendor or an allocated state. Context pack ownership rows list exactly two tables for S5. Legacy Data table rows: recovery_case, assignment, v_ace_npa_asset, decision_log_entry, v_ace_score, rule_row.
owner_role: S5 rwb-asset service owner with the data steward of the Asset module
proposed: Hold the chosen vendor, the basis and the score as facts of the local decision record and answer them on the asset read, add no column, and raise a DB change only if the owner decides the vendor must be queryable as a listing field.

title: No requirement of the module covers vendor allocation and the plan carries no requirement id for either slice
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E4-023, metadata table with no Requirement row); _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json (the reqs list of both slices, empty); Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (section Requirements served, rows REQ-S5-001 to REQ-S5-010); Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (T8 requirement traceability)
section: APP s18 Traceability; the reqs key of both fragments; CON s18 Traceability
description: The traceability of the two stories needs one sourced requirement and no source provides one for this feature. The legacy metadata table of RWB-E4-023 carries Epic, Module, Feature, Process, Priority, Depends on and Decision and no requirement row, the plan's reqs list for both slices is empty, the FSD Requirements served table gives ten requirements of which the closest, REQ-S5-005, is about publishing listings to the bank's channel and the auction portal and none is about choosing a vendor, and TSD S5 T8 traces only REQ-S5-001 to REQ-S5-010 against FEAT-AST-01 and FEAT-AST-08 with the story column reading Written one epic ahead. Both stories therefore trace to the feature and record the empty plan list rather than inventing an identifier.
evidence: Legacy metadata table of RWB-E4-023 lists seven rows and no Requirement. FSD S5 Requirements served gives REQ-S5-001 to REQ-S5-010, all mapped to epics E3 and E4 with REQ-S5-005 about listings and REQ-S5-006 about auction rounds. TSD S5 T8 tabulates REQ-S5-001 to REQ-S5-010 against FEAT-AST-01 and FEAT-AST-08 only. Plan reqs lists of RWB-S5-E4023-APP and RWB-S5-E4023-CON are empty.
owner_role: S5 rwb-asset service owner with the business analyst of the Asset module
proposed: Trace both slices to FEAT-AST-14 of the FSD S5 A2.14 and let step D1 add a requirement row for vendor allocation to the next version of the module requirements.

title: The FSD S5, the TSD S5 and the Epics 3 to 8 Specification that the two slices read are in review with empty sign-off tables and the realigned stories have no approval
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (document control, document sign-off); Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (document control, document sign-off); Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 (document control); Template and Rules v1 R8.1; AGENTS.md rules 9 and 10
section: Metadata row Status of both stories; APP s3 Preconditions; CON s3 Preconditions
description: The sources of both slices are not approved. The FSD S5 is at version 3 in review with an empty sign-off table and the TSD S5 is at version 2 in review with an empty sign-off table, the Epics 3 to 8 Specification that carries the feature extract is at version 3 without approval, and the run of D-RCV-60 has no human approval step, so the missing approval is recorded as an assumption, both stories carry Status Draft (realignment v1) and the work continues. No behaviour and no value of either story depends on a signature, and no status of a source document is changed.
evidence: FSD S5 document control gives Status In review and its document sign-off table has empty Name, Signature and Date cells; TSD S5 v2 document control gives Status In review and its sign-off table is empty; Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 carries a document control block with no approval; Template and Rules v1 R8.1 asks every new document for a change-log row naming D-RCV-60 and the tool line; AGENTS.md rule 9 says a missing approval is recorded as an assumption and the work continues in Draft.
owner_role: Solution architect and the business owner of the Asset module
proposed: Keep both stories at Draft (realignment v1) and let the verification loop collect the sign-offs before any status changes.

title: No source publishes an operation for the allocation step itself and the panel element, its field names and the allocation reference have no published shape
source: _work/msr/context/S5.md (ownership rows of S5: six REST operations; connection matrix); Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (appendix T-A.1 endpoint inventory, T-A.2 endpoint detail); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E4-023, Endpoints table); Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (A2.14.2 integration points Partner portal); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-DIS-30, R-DIS-31 Systems column)
section: CON s1 Story; s3 Preconditions; s7 AC2 to AC4; s12.1; s12.2; s12.5; s12.8; s13; s19; APP s12.1
description: The contract baseline has to declare a surface for a step that no source gives an operation. The legacy Endpoints table of RWB-E4-023 names POST assets listings and GET asset only, and neither is the allocation; the ownership rows give S5 six operations of which four belong to other steps, and the TSD S5 T-A.1 gives five, of which the listing and the round are the pricing and auction stories'. The Systems column of both rules names the Rules component and the Partner Portal, the FSD names the partner portal as the integration point, and no source gives the partner operation, its request, its answer, its field names, its error set or the allocation reference the read must answer. The baseline therefore declares the two asset reads, the three consumed REST rows, the panel element on the call type of the matrix, the two workflow signals and their fields, and carries the placeholder wherever a name is missing.
evidence: Legacy Endpoints table rows: POST /api/recovery/v1/assets/{assetId}/listings access C and GET /api/recovery/v1/assets/{assetId} access R. Context pack ownership rows: GET assets, GET assets/{assetId}, GET assets/{assetKey}, POST assets/{assetId}/listings, POST assets/{assetKey}/listings, POST listings/{listingId}/rounds. TSD S5 T-A.1 five endpoints with API-S5-005 first in E4. Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DIS-30 and R-DIS-31 Systems: Rules component, Partner Portal.
owner_role: S5 rwb-asset tech lead with the owner of S9 rwb-partner
proposed: Declare the two reads and the three consumed rows, declare the panel element and the two signals with the placeholder names, and let the tag wait for rwb-partner to publish the activity name and its answer fields.
